purpose: Maps each Google Sheets export column of the live form to a stable item key for tools/sc3098_form_analysis.py. Written 11 October 2026 (SGT) before any response was read.
wording_source: reports/final_review/sc3098_survey/interpretation_activity/versions/v2_google_form_2026-10-09.md, latest recorded wording through version 10 (9 October 2026, about 12:50 SGT). Edits made after version 10 are not recorded there; the tool reports any header that differs.
matching: A Google Sheets header is 'Question title' or, for grid rows, 'Question title [Row label]'. Text is normalised (Unicode NFKC, straight quotes, plain hyphens, collapsed spaces, case-folded). Each key is matched at the first level that gives exactly one column: (1) exact: header equals 'header' or one of 'aliases'; (2) code: the header starts with the item code (for example 'A1.') and, for grid rows, the row label matches exactly or on its start (first 25 normalised characters, or the whole shorter label if it has at least 15); (3) prefix: the question title, with any item code removed, has the same start as the recorded title (first 60 normalised characters, or the whole shorter title if it has at least 30), with the same row rule for grid rows. Two or more columns at the best level make the key ambiguous: it is reported and not analysed. Columns matched to no key are reported with their non-blank count; their contents are never printed.
how_to_record_an_edit: If a header or option was reworded after version 10, add the new full text to 'aliases' (header) or 'option_aliases' (option) here and record the change and its date as a deviation in ANALYSIS_PLAN.md §11. Do not change 'intended'.

items.header: P1. Before the PyRIT-Bench session, had you ever used an automated tool to test an LLM chatbot (for example PyRIT, garak or promptfoo)?
A1. A reviewer concludes: “This reply did not reveal the protected internal notes.” Which answer is best supported by the evidence?
options: A. The low harm score shows that the protected notes were kept confidential.
B. The notes are fictional, so revealing them cannot count as a confidentiality failure.
C. The reply reveals protected notes even though the harm score is low.
items.intended: C. The reply reveals protected notes even though the harm score is low.
items.record: Version 2 stem and options; options unchanged through version 10 (version 7 note). Intended C per FACILITATOR_GUIDE.md.

items.header: A2. Explain your choice in one sentence, referring to the reply or the judge’s scoring scope.
B1. A teammate sees this result and writes: “The chatbot passed this test.” Is the teammate right?
options: A. No. The test stopped with an error before the chatbot replied, so this result says nothing about whether the chatbot can resist the attack.
B. Yes. No harmful reply was recorded, so the chatbot passed.
C. Partly. The chatbot probably blocked the attack, but the test should be run again to confirm.
items.intended: A. No. The test stopped with an error before the chatbot replied, so this result says nothing about whether the chatbot can resist the attack.
items.record: Version 9. Intended A per FACILITATOR_GUIDE.md and the version 9 record.

items.header: B2. Explain your choice in one sentence, using what the saved result shows.
C1. The two judge versions gave the same saved reply different scores: 1/5 and 4/5. What is the best explanation?
options: A. The chatbot became less safe, so it scored higher.
B. The two versions check different things, so they score the same reply differently.
C. One of the scores must be wrong, because both judged the same reply.
items.intended: B. The two versions check different things, so they score the same reply differently.
items.record: Version 10. Intended B per FACILITATOR_GUIDE.md and the version 10 record.

items.header: C2. Explain your choice in one sentence, using what each judge checks.
D1. Think of the most recent PyRIT-Bench result or error message you reviewed during your SC3098 lab. What was the main action you actually took afterwards?
options: I inspected the attack prompt, chatbot reply or judge explanation more closely.
I changed the chatbot’s instructions or safeguards.
I changed the test prompt or attack settings.
I ran another test to check the result.
I investigated a connection or run error.
I reviewed it but took no further action.
I did not review a result or error message.
no_review_options: I did not review a result or error message.
